cve_summary: Incorrect returning of an error code in the index.c:read_entry() function leads to a double free in libgit2 before v0.26.2, which allows an attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted repository index file.
commit_message:
index: convert `read_entry` to return entry size via an out-param

The function `read_entry` does not conform to our usual coding style of
returning stuff via the out parameter and to use the return value for
reporting errors. Due to most of our code conforming to that pattern, it
has become quite natural for us to actually return `-1` in case there is
any error, which has also slipped in with commit 5625d86b9 (index:
support index v4, 2016-05-17). As the function returns an `size_t` only,
though, the return value is wrapped around, causing the caller of
`read_tree` to continue with an invalid index entry. Ultimately, this
can lead to a double-free.

Improve code and fix the bug by converting the function to return the
index entry size via an out parameter and only using the return value to
indicate errors.

Reported-by: Krishna Ram Prakash R <krp@gtux.in>
Reported-by: Vivek Parikh <viv0411.parikh@gmail.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: Parses a git index from a given buffer and populates the provided git_index structure.

Parameters:
index (git_index *): Pointer to the git_index structure to be populated.
buffer (const char *): Pointer to the buffer containing the index data.
buffer_size (size_t): Size of the buffer in bytes.

Returns: int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: The function first checks if the buffer has sufficient size for the index header and footer. It calculates the SHA1 checksum of the buffer contents and reads the index header. It then processes each index entry, inserting it into the index structure and handling case sensitivity as specified. The function also reads any extensions present in the buffer. Finally, it verifies the calculated checksum against the expected checksum from the buffer, updates the index checksum, and sorts the entries if necessary. If any errors occur during processing, appropriate error codes are returned.
"""
